A draft and uploads may be preparatory effects; public publication waits for all required outputs of that release owner. Exact draft timing must be specified with the implementation. This is Callisto's policy, not a universal ecosystem order.\n\nWithin Callisto's release-operation graph, one physical tag, forge release or upload has one owner even when several distributions share it. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain package-owner-defined behavior and environment. Callisto does not inspect, rewrite, suppress or reject those hooks; any effects they initiate are outside Callisto's graph and remain the package owner's responsibility. For example, NAPI `prepublishOnly` may publish platform packages or GitHub assets while Callisto also performs configured release effects.\n\nA retry retains the authorized roster and observes every remaining effect, even when its tag or some registry files already exist. Keep execution state in memory; the immutable intent, original artifact manifest and providers supply recovery evidence. No journal, automatic version bump, destructive rollback or changed replacement bytes under an already-published version.\n\nPyPI completion is the declared file set for the release, not the first matching wheel or sdist. Required platform packages must exist before their npm owner publishes. Missing, conflicting, yanked and unobservable results must not be collapsed into complete success. Use hashes where needed to distinguish intended files from conflicting bytes; do not make an unapproved universal registry-checksum requirement a v1 gate.\n\nRegistry identity is separate from read/upload routes and native authentication configuration. Specify public PyPI first; decide authenticated private indexes and HTML-only indexes explicitly. Mutable npm dist-tags are channel labels, not distribution versions; channel verification/promotion policy is an owner decision, not implicit rollback.\n\n## Future compatibility examples\n\n- Go: a source tag is a publication effect; a v2+ module generally has a new major-qualified module path, and subdirectory modules need their native tag prefix. Do not require every ecosystem to publish before its source tag or carry its version in a manifest.\n- NuGet: package-version normalization differs from SemVer; package version is not assembly/file version. A single package can contain runtime-identifier and target-framework assets. Do not assume every native target is a Rust triple or every platform is a separate distribution.\n- Cross-language wrappers: native libraries, subprocess tools and generated bindings are concrete inputs to a native distribution, not foreign package-manager dependency entries. Building Rust into a Python wheel does not by itself require a crates.io publication.\n\nThese are model checks only. Go/NuGet discovery, rewriting, packing, authentication and publication remain deferred.\n\n## Prior art and research limits\n\n| Tool | Established approach | Boundary relevant to Callisto |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Changesets | npm/pnpm graph-based publication, then tags for successful publications | Native JS release semantics, not a cross-registry transaction. [Publisher](https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/packages/cli/src/commands/publish/index.ts) |\n| Knope | Several versioned files can form one release package | Cargo+Python ownership stays simple; Python dependency rewriting is not supported by its documented format handler. [Ownership](https://knope.tech/tutorials/releasing-multiple-packages/), [formats](https://knope.tech/reference/config-file/packages/) |\n| Nx Release | Project identities, release groups and ecosystem VersionActions/publishers | Reuse the separation, not the general build framework. Its Rust recipe still documents a legacy-versioning restriction; current plugin compatibility needs a runtime check. [Configuration](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-json), [Rust recipe](https://nx.dev/docs/kb/publish-rust-crates) |\n| release-please | Polyglot strategies, native workspace plugins and separate registry publishing | Its example publishes npm after tags/releases already exist; that is not Callisto's required completion policy. [Manifest model](https://github.com/googleapis/release-please/blob/main/docs/manifest-releaser.md) |\n\nSources checked on 2026-09-26: [Maturin version authority](https://www.maturin.rs/metadata), [pnpm workspace transformations](https://pnpm.io/workspaces), [catalogs](https://pnpm.io/catalogs), [Python name normalization](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/name-normalization/), [PEP 440](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/version-specifiers/), [PyPI one-file uploads](https://docs.pypi.org/api/upload/), [per-file index evidence](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/), [NAPI publication hooks](https://napi.rs/docs/cli/pre-publish), [Go module versions](https://go.dev/doc/modules/version-numbers), [NuGet normalization](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/concepts/package-versioning), [NuGet native assets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/create-packages/native-files-in-net-packages).\n\nCompetitor release workflows were inspected, not executed. Fresh co-located static and dynamic Cargo/Maturin discovery fixtures both reproduced E007. Native pack/install tests and partial-upload fault injection remain planned; see [the findings register](../projects/V1-FINDINGS.md).\n\n## Non-goals\n\nNo universal package manager, build scheduler, five public graph types, arbitrary interoperability inference, external service graph, cross-registry atomic transaction, public adapter framework or persisted execution-state mechanism. Expand the model only when a supported fixture demonstrates a missing responsibility.\n# Architecture decision records\n\n- [1. Changesets-compatible change records](0001-changesets-compatible-change-records.md) — `.changeset/*.md` in `@changesets/cli`'s format, commit inference opt-in; guardrail: do not make Conventional Commits the primary input or change the file format without a new ADR.\n- [2. The committed version decision is the release authority](0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md) — CI verifies the merged commit against the decision `callisto version --emit-decision` committed; guardrail: do not re-derive cascade or group policy after merge without a new ADR.\n- [3. Reruns observe and adopt landed effects; no persisted execution state](0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md) — every run observes providers and adopts what landed, state stays in memory; guardrail: do not add a persisted execution state file or recovery commands without a new ADR.\n- [4. Ecosystem tools publish and own authentication](0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) — `cargo`, the npm-family tools, `twine` and `gh` publish with their own credentials; guardrail: do not add native registry clients or a credential pre-flight without a new ADR.\n- [5. System git only](0005-system-git-only.md) — every Git command in the `callisto` binary runs the system `git`; guardrail: do not add gix or a second Git backend without a new ADR.\n- [6. moon integrates through a proto plugin, not a WASM extension](0006-moon-through-proto-plugin-not-wasm-extension.md) — moon users install the native CLI with a proto TOML plugin; guardrail: do not add a moon WASM extension or WASM build without a new ADR.\n- [7. Platform packages are owned through optionalDependencies and release with their owner](0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md) — an `os`+`cpu` package with one owner releases with that owner; guardrail: do not require fixed-group entries or explicit config for platform packages without a new ADR.\n- [8. Format-preserving manifest writes gated by ApplyPermit](0008-format-preserving-writes-gated-by-apply-permit.md) — `toml_edit` and fingerprinted JSON through `atomic_write(&ApplyPermit)`; guardrail: do not use typed serde round-trips for TOML, unfingerprinted `package.json` rewrites, regex edits or unpermitted writes without a new ADR.\n- [9. A tag's identity is its commit and being annotated](0009-tag-identity-is-commit-and-annotation.md) — an existing annotated tag on the planned commit is adopted whatever its message; guardrail: do not compare annotation text or accept lightweight tags without a new ADR.\n- [10. The workspace resolves natively after `version` or `snapshot`](0010-native-resolution-after-version.md) — a co-released dependent's spec is always raised to the new version and lockfiles refresh by default; guardrail: do not go back to rewriting only out-of-range specs or make lockfile refresh opt-in without a new ADR.\n- [11. Directory-keyed packages and promotion-aware history](0011-directory-keyed-package-identity.md) — the directory key survives display promotion; new default tags use the promoted display id and historical bare records use an ownership fallback; guardrail: do not derive paths or persisted keys from the display id without a new ADR.\n- [12. Canonical distribution references and explicit release ownership](0012-canonical-distribution-release-ownership.md) — proposed v1 correction; not accepted or implemented. Separates native distribution identities, version authority and shared effects while preserving deliberate historical migration.\n\n## Rules\n\n- An ADR records an architecturally significant decision that had a credible alternative.\n- `Proposed` until the PR that implements it merges, then `Accepted`.\n- A changed decision gets a new ADR with `Status: Supersedes N`. The old file moves to `docs/adr/superseded/` with `Status: Superseded by M`. Agents do not load that folder.\n- Every reason cites a source (commit, PR, historical doc). If none exists, write \"Reason not recorded\".\n- Behaviour belongs in `docs/specs/`; coding rules belong in `AGENTS.md`.\n"}}

1	//! Pure argv construction for "publish a package to its registry", plus
     2	//! subprocess-output classification for the same three ecosystems (Cargo,
     3	//! npm, PyPI).
     4	//!
     5	//! This module owns exactly two questions per ecosystem: *what command do we
     6	//! run* (given package/plan facts and already-detected environment facts --
     7	//! never a [`callisto_model::CommandRunner`] call of its own) and *what did
     8	//! the finished command's output mean*. Actually invoking the command, and
     9	//! any retry/backoff policy around a failed attempt, is the caller's job --
    10	//! see the durable release executor's single production publish path.
    11	//!
    12	//! A small amount of local filesystem reading happens here (the Cargo
    13	//! on-disk version check, npm package-manager detection from lockfiles, the
    14	//! PyPI interpreter's PATH lookup) -- that's "gathering the facts needed to
    15	//! build the right argv", not executing a publish. It never shells out.
    16	
    17	use std::ffi::OsStr;
    18	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    19	use std::time::Duration;
    20	
    21	use callisto_manifests::WorkspaceCargoResolver;
    22	use callisto_model::{CommandOutput, Ecosystem, NpmAccess, PackageId, PublishOutcome, RegistryError, Version};
    23	
    24	use crate::error::{GraphError, ReleasePreconditionRequirement};
    25	
    26	/// Default fallback wait (seconds) when a registry does not supply a
    27	/// `retry_after` value and the classifier cannot parse one from output.
    28	const DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 60;
    29	
    30	/// One subprocess invocation: program, args, and working directory. Building
    31	/// this is the entire job of the `*_publish_argv` functions below --
    32	/// executing it is the caller's.
    33	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    34	pub struct Argv {
    35	    pub program: String,
    36	    pub args: Vec<String>,
    37	    pub cwd: PathBuf,
    38	}
    39	
    40	// ---------------------------------------------------------------- cargo
    41	
    42	/// Builds the exact `cargo publish` argv for one crate: `--manifest-path`
    43	/// (so the caller can keep the workspace root as its own working directory)
    44	/// plus `--locked`, so a stale `Cargo.lock` fails the publish immediately
    45	/// instead of `cargo` silently re-resolving one at publish time.
    46	/// `registry_key` is `Some` only for a non-default registry -- crates.io is
    47	/// the implicit default and never needs `--registry`.
    48	///
    49	/// Before returning, verifies that the on-disk `Cargo.toml` version under
    50	/// `package_dir` (resolving `version.workspace = true` against the
    51	/// workspace root's `[workspace.package].version` when present) matches
    52	/// `version` -- this is the one behavior `SubprocessRegistryClient` had that
    53	/// the durable release executor's own `dispatch_registry` had silently
    54	/// dropped: it catches the common mistake of running `release execute`
    55	/// without first running `callisto version`, which would otherwise silently
    56	/// publish the old on-disk version.
    57	pub fn cargo_publish_argv(
    58	    workspace_root: &Path,
    59	    package_dir: &Path,
    60	    package_name: &str,
    61	    version: &Version,
    62	    registry_key: Option<&str>,
    63	) -> Result<Argv, GraphError> {
    64	    verify_cargo_ondisk_version(workspace_root, package_dir, package_name, version)?;
    65	
    66	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
    67	    let mut args = vec![
    68	        "publish".to_string(),
    69	        "--manifest-path".to_string(),
    70	        manifest_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
    71	        "--locked".to_string(),
    72	    ];
    73	    if let Some(reg) = registry_key {
    74	        args.push("--registry".to_string());
    75	        args.push(reg.to_string());
    76	    }
    77	    Ok(Argv {
    78	        program: "cargo".to_string(),
    79	        args,
    80	        cwd: workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
    81	    })
    82	}
    83	
    84	fn verify_cargo_ondisk_version(
    85	    workspace_root: &Path,
    86	    package_dir: &Path,
    87	    package_name: &str,
    88	    planned: &Version,
    89	) -> Result<(), GraphError> {
    90	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
    91	    let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&manifest_path).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
    92	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
    93	        message: error.to_string(),
    94	    })?;
    95	    // Parse only the [package].version field -- no need for full CST. A
    96	    // permissive `toml::Value` intermediate rather than a direct `String`
    97	    // deserialization, because `version.workspace = true` (Cargo's
    98	    // workspace-version-inheritance syntax) parses `version` as a table, not
    99	    // a string.
   100	    let parsed = toml::from_str::<toml::Value>(&contents).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   101	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
   102	        message: error.to_string(),
   103	    })?;
   104	    let version_value =
   105	        parsed
   106	            .get("package")
   107	            .and_then(|p| p.get("version"))
   108	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   109	                path: manifest_path.clone(),
   110	                message: "missing [package].version".to_string(),
   111	            })?;
   112	
   113	    let on_disk = if let Some(s) = version_value.as_str() {
   114	        s.to_string()
   115	    } else if version_value.get("workspace").and_then(toml::Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
   116	        let root_manifest_path = workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml");
   117	        let resolver = WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_manifest_path)?;
   118	        let ws_version = resolver
   119	            .workspace_version()?
   120	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   121	                path: root_manifest_path.clone(),
   122	                message: "`version.workspace = true` but the workspace root has no [workspace.package].version"
   123	                    .to_string(),
   124	            })?;
   125	        ws_version.render().to_string()
   126	    } else {
   127	        return Err(GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   128	            path: manifest_path,
   129	            message: "[package].version is neither a string nor a `{ workspace = true }` table".to_string(),
   130	        });
   131	    };
   132	
   133	    let found = Version::parse(&on_disk, planned.grammar())?;
   134	    if found != *planned {
   135	        return Err(GraphError::OnDiskVersionDrift {
   136	            package: PackageId::Prefixed {
   137	                ecosystem: Ecosystem::Cargo,
   138	                name: package_name.to_string(),
   139	            },
   140	            expected: planned.clone(),
   141	            found,
   142	        });
   143	    }
   144	    Ok(())
   145	}

   147	// ------------------------------------------------------------------ npm
   148	
   149	/// The npm-compatible package manager a workspace uses, detected from
   150	/// lockfile presence. Each one needs a materially different invocation to
   151	/// publish a single named package out of a monorepo -- see
   152	/// [`npm_publish_argv`].
   153	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   154	pub enum NpmPackageManager {
   155	    Pnpm,
   156	    Yarn,
   157	    Bun,
   158	    Npm,
   159	}
   160	
   161	/// Detects the npm-compatible package manager for `workspace_root` from
   162	/// lockfile presence. Detection priority: pnpm > yarn > bun > npm (default).
   163	///
   164	/// This is real, live-today correctness content: the durable release
   165	/// executor's `dispatch_registry` used to hardcode plain `npm publish`
   166	/// regardless of which package manager a workspace actually uses, so a pnpm
   167	/// or yarn workspace published with the wrong tool.
   168	pub fn detect_npm_package_manager(workspace_root: &Path) -> NpmPackageManager {
   169	    if workspace_root.join("pnpm-lock.yaml").exists() {
   170	        NpmPackageManager::Pnpm
   171	    } else if workspace_root.join("yarn.lock").exists() {
   172	        NpmPackageManager::Yarn
   173	    } else if workspace_root.join("bun.lockb").exists() || workspace_root.join("bun.lock").exists() {
   174	        // bun.lockb is the legacy binary lockfile format; bun.lock (text) is
   175	        // written by Bun >= 1.1.1. Both signal a bun-managed workspace.
   176	        NpmPackageManager::Bun
   177	    } else {
   178	        NpmPackageManager::Npm
   179	    }
   180	}

   182	/// Builds the npm-ecosystem publish argv for one package, given the
   183	/// already-detected `package_manager` (see [`detect_npm_package_manager`]).
   184	///
   185	/// | Package manager | Program | Base args                                  |
   186	/// |------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------|
   187	/// | Pnpm             | `pnpm`  | `publish --filter=<name> --no-git-checks`  |
   188	/// | Yarn             | `yarn`  | `workspace <name> npm publish`             |
   189	/// | Bun              | `bun`   | `publish` (run from `package_dir`)         |
   190	/// | Npm              | `npm`   | `publish --workspace=<name>`               |
   191	///
   192	/// `--filter=`/`--workspace=` use the joined form so the name cannot be
   193	/// re-read as an option. Yarn takes the name positionally and has no joined
   194	/// spelling, so there it rests on `ReleasePackageId`'s leading-`-` rejection.
   195	///
   196	/// `tag`/`access`/`registry` are appended to every variant's base args.
   197	/// `package_dir` is only used for bun: it has no `--filter`/`--workspace`
   198	/// flag to target one package by name, so it alone must run from the
   199	/// package's own directory rather than the workspace root.
   200	pub fn npm_publish_argv(
   201	    workspace_root: &Path,
   202	    package_dir: &Path,
   203	    package_name: &str,
   204	    package_manager: NpmPackageManager,
   205	    tag: Option<&str>,
   206	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
   207	    registry: Option<&str>,
   208	) -> Argv {
   209	    let extra = npm_publish_flags(package_name, tag, access, registry);
   210	
   211	    let (program, mut args, cwd) = match package_manager {
   212	        NpmPackageManager::Pnpm => (
   213	            "pnpm",
   214	            vec![
   215	                "publish".to_string(),
   216	                // `--filter=<name>`, not `--filter <name>`: the joined form
   217	                // cannot be re-read as an option even if a name slipped past
   218	                // `ReleasePackageId`'s charset rule.
   219	                format!("--filter={package_name}"),
   220	                // pnpm >= 7 refuses to publish from a dirty working tree by
   221	                // default. After `callisto version` stages manifest bumps,
   222	                // the tree is always dirty until the operator commits, so
   223	                // this bypasses the git-status check.
   224	                "--no-git-checks".to_string(),
   225	            ],
   226	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   227	        ),
   228	        NpmPackageManager::Yarn => (
   229	            "yarn",
   230	            vec![
   231	                "workspace".to_string(),
   232	                package_name.to_string(),
   233	                "npm".to_string(),
   234	                "publish".to_string(),
   235	            ],
   236	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   237	        ),
   238	        NpmPackageManager::Bun => ("bun", vec!["publish".to_string()], workspace_root.join(package_dir)),
   239	        NpmPackageManager::Npm => (
   240	            "npm",
   241	            vec!["publish".to_string(), format!("--workspace={package_name}")],
   242	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   243	        ),
   244	    };
   245	    args.extend(extra);
   246	    Argv {
   247	        program: program.to_string(),
   248	        args,
   249	        cwd,
   250	    }
   251	}

   225	pub(super) struct Comparison<'a> {
   226	    /// Declared files the index lacks.

   228	    /// Declared files the index holds yanked.
   229	    pub(super) yanked: Vec<&'a str>,

   231	    pub(super) differing: Vec<&'a str>,

   233	    pub(super) extras: Vec<&'a str>,
   234	}

docs/publishing.md:5:Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.
docs/publishing.md:9:## npm
docs/publishing.md:13:### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`
docs/publishing.md:15:Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the protected `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:
docs/publishing.md:18:- name: Authenticate with npm registry
docs/publishing.md:19:  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
docs/publishing.md:26:`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.
docs/publishing.md:30:`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:
docs/publishing.md:36:    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
docs/publishing.md:43:`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.
docs/publishing.md:56:Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.
docs/publishing.md:60:## Cargo (crates.io)
docs/publishing.md:69:Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. In this repo, inject it only into `execute`.
docs/publishing.md:73:## Python (PyPI)
docs/publishing.md:85:Map the generated workflow's `PYPI_TOKEN` secret to `TWINE_PASSWORD` in the publishing job. The secret name alone does not configure Twine.
docs/publishing.md:89:Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.
docs/publishing.md:91:Native publish hooks, including `prepare` and `prepublishOnly`, run unchanged with their usual publishing environment.
docs/publishing.md:93:### Current Python support limits
docs/publishing.md:97:- Co-located Cargo/Maturin projects fail discovery with E007, including Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions.
docs/publishing.md:99:- A sealed build is used only by the generated build-matrix workflow, which builds in a `build-python` job without credentials and seals the files in the manifest. The generated execute job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. Sealing is opt-in at execution: a manifest that seals no Python files, or no manifest at all, builds in the executing job and warns. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. A workspace whose only release work is Python uses the single-job workflow, which installs pinned `build` and `twine` before the release step, and is not sealed. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).
docs/publishing.md:100:- A release can only be completed for 14 days after its first file; after that, PyPI [refuses new files](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/) and the release needs a new version.
docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md:11:| SYS-MATURIN | `Package::version_grammar`: two fresh co-located Cargo/Maturin repos, with matching static versions and Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions, both reproduce E007 from init/status. Separate-directory fixtures did not cover this layout. | T07 | WS-ID-09; proposed version authority |
docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md:16:- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.
docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md:17:- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes or the desired npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete when every built file is on the index by name; sealing the file set in a build job and comparing digests of earlier uploads is the rest of T09. Universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md:18:- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. Record exercised versus skipped paths; do not mark the missing Cargo test as the remaining v1 blocker (T12).
docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md:19:- Fresh local Cargo/npm/PyPI repositories completed documented setup through release dry-run; npm packing and Cargo package inventory passed. Python artifact build was blocked on sandbox network access to `setuptools`, and no timings, credentials, registry publication or hosted release were exercised. The under-ten-minute first-published-release goal therefore remains unverified (T12-DX).
docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md:26:Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only indexes, npm channel promotion, universal registry checksum requirements and automatic wrapper bump severity also need a support/policy decision. The proposed model keeps room for them without making them required implementations.
docs/releasing.md:3:How a Callisto-managed release moves from changeset to published package.
docs/releasing.md:5:For registry credential setup (npm, crates.io, PyPI), see [`publishing.md`](publishing.md).
docs/releasing.md:11:`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.
docs/releasing.md:20:`cargo`, `npm`, `twine`, and `gh` report their own authentication failures. With the original release intent, the executor can adopt matching completed effects.
docs/releasing.md:39:- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): a release PR, then plan -> build -> publish. The build covers configured targets and artifact slots.
docs/releasing.md:42:Generated actions configure npm and Twine authentication during execution. Manual workflows must configure native authentication as described in [publishing.md](publishing.md).
docs/releasing.md:46:- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
docs/releasing.md:47:- Co-located Cargo/Maturin manifests fail discovery with E007.
docs/releasing.md:49:- Registry-only npm and PyPI releases need no artifact slots.
docs/releasing.md:51:The default branch is the approval boundary: a merge to it publishes. Protect it with a rule that requires pull requests and reviews (GitHub -> Settings -> Rules). Init prints this reminder after writing the file.
docs/releasing.md:57:- Cargo `bin` targets build with `cargo build --release --locked`. Other products, such as `cdylib`s, need a manual workflow.
docs/releasing.md:59:- Native npm lifecycle hooks run unchanged, including any owner-defined publishing or forge effects. Those effects are outside Callisto's release graph.
docs/releasing.md:118:Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes, the npm dist-tag, or a complete Python wheel/sdist set. A partial PyPI upload can therefore be mistaken for a complete version. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).
docs/releasing.md:124:## Platform-package publish order
docs/releasing.md:126:`callisto release execute` follows the derived operation DAG, not a fixed global Cargo -> npm -> PyPI pipeline. Native dependency edges and attached npm platform prerequisites constrain that order. Platform packages publish before their npm owner.
docs/releasing.md:128:A napi-rs distribution can publish N platform-specific npm packages plus one owner package whose `optionalDependencies` pin their versions. Maturin instead produces Python wheels and optionally an sdist under one PyPI distribution/version; those are files, not npm platform packages.
docs/releasing.md:131:- **A platform dependency is missing from the selection entirely**: planning refuses (`ReleaseSelectionInvalid`, "select it too") before anything is published.
docs/releasing.md:133:For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.

---
callisto-cli: minor
---

A Python release that stopped partway is completed on rerun. Only the files PyPI lacks are uploaded, and the release counts as published only when both the wheel and the sdist it builds are on the index, so no tag is created for a half-published release. Uploads name their files instead of a dist glob, so a stale dist directory is no longer published.

Breaking: `callisto_graph`'s `registry_argv::pypi_publish_argv` is replaced by `pypi_build_argv` and `pypi_upload_argv`.
---
callisto-cli: minor
---

A release workflow that builds Python distributions in a job without registry credentials now publishes exactly those files. The generated build-matrix workflow gains a `build-python` job, the manifest records each file's name, size and sha256, and a file PyPI already holds under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release before any upload. Python builds also set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` to the release commit time.
---
callisto-cli: patch
---

Generated release workflows now install the Python build and upload tools they need. A workspace that publishes to PyPI no longer depends on `twine` being preinstalled on the runner.

1	# Publishing: registry authentication
     2	
     3	Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).
     4	
     5	Callisto delegates authentication to `cargo`, `npm`/`pnpm`, and `twine`. Configure credentials for those tools in the publishing job.
     6	
     7	---
     8	
     9	## npm
    10	
    11	Two supported patterns.
    12	
    13	### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`
    14	
    15	Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the protected `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:
    16	
    17	```yaml
    18	- name: Authenticate with npm registry
    19	  run: npm config set //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken $NPM_TOKEN
    20	  env:
    21	    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
    22	
    23	- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
    24	```
    25	
    26	`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.
    27	
    28	### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`
    29	
    30	`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:
    31	
    32	```yaml
    33	- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    34	  with:
    35	    node-version: '20'
    36	    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
    37	
    38	- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
    39	  env:
    40	    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
    41	```
    42	
    43	`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` needs an `.npmrc` entry containing `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`. `setup-node` writes it only when `registry-url` is set. The environment variable alone does not authenticate npm.
    44	
    45	### Choosing a pattern
    46	
    47	| Criterion | Pattern A (`NPM_TOKEN` + manual step) | Pattern B (`setup-node` + `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`) |
    48	| --- | --- | --- |
    49	| Depends on `actions/setup-node` | No | Yes — `registry-url` must be set |
    50	| Node.js version management | Separate step or pre-installed | Handled by `setup-node` |
    51	| Recommended when | `execute` job doesn't otherwise need Node setup | `execute` job already uses `setup-node` |
    52	| Release-PR action receives the token | Never | Never |
    53

    55	
    56	Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.
    57	
    58	---
    59	
    60	## Cargo (crates.io)
    61	
    62	Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:
    63	
    64	```yaml
    65	env:
    66	  CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
    67	```
    68	
    69	Cargo reads this variable directly; no `.cargo/credentials` step is needed. In this repo, inject it only into `execute`.
    70	
    71	---
    72	
    73	## Python (PyPI)
    74	
    75	Publishing uses `twine upload`, which reads `TWINE_USERNAME` (`__token__` for a PyPI API token) and `TWINE_PASSWORD` (the token value):
    76	
    77	```yaml
    78	env:
    79	  TWINE_USERNAME: __token__
    80	  TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}

    10	
    11	Two supported patterns.
    12	
    13	### Pattern A: manual `.npmrc` via `NPM_TOKEN`
    14	
    15	Set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. Add this only in the protected `execute` job, immediately before the publish step:
    16

    18	- name: Authenticate with npm registry

    20	  env:
    21	    NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
    22	
    23	- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
    24	```
    25	
    26	`npm config set` writes the user-level `.npmrc` for later publish calls in the job. The version-PR action receives no token.
    27	
    28	### Pattern B: `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url`
    29	
    30	`actions/setup-node`, given `registry-url`, writes a project-level `.npmrc` that reads the token from `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`:
    31

    33	- uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    34	  with:
    35	    node-version: '20'
    36	    registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

    39	  env:

# V1 system findings

Baseline: main `07154021c` (0.10.2). This is an open findings register, not an implemented behavior spec: it lists unshipped defects and evidence gaps only. [Roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [execution guide](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Confirmed means reproduced against the main binary or established by the cited code path; the evidence column distinguishes them. No hosted publication, competitor execution or fresh-repo timing run has been performed.

## Open confirmed defects

| Finding | Evidence and consequence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-MATURIN | `Package::version_grammar`: two fresh co-located Cargo/Maturin repos, with matching static versions and Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions, both reproduce E007 from init/status. Separate-directory fixtures did not cover this layout. | T07 | WS-ID-09; proposed version authority |
| SYS-PYROUTES | `PreparedRegistryBinding.endpoint` is reused for simple-index observation and Twine upload. Source-confirmed single-route assumption; servers with distinct read/upload routes cannot generally use one override. Public defaults use separate native routes. | T09-ROUTES | REL-PUB-04/08; private-index policy |

## Integration risks and evidence gaps

- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.
- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes or the desired npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete when every built file is on the index by name; sealing the file set in a build job and comparing digests of earlier uploads is the rest of T09. Universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. Record exercised versus skipped paths; do not mark the missing Cargo test as the remaining v1 blocker (T12).
- Fresh local Cargo/npm/PyPI repositories completed documented setup through release dry-run; npm packing and Cargo package inventory passed. Python artifact build was blocked on sandbox network access to `setuptools`, and no timings, credentials, registry publication or hosted release were exercised. The under-ten-minute first-published-release goal therefore remains unverified (T12-DX).
- Go v2/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are architecture examples only, not production support or new v1 gates (T07/T08/T12).

## Owner policy, not a defect verdict

Commit inference can produce pending bumps while `hasChangesets` is false; managed release-PR decisions then return noop. Committed verification also requires a consumed changeset, as ADR 2 states. Decide whether inferred-only/manual version releases belong in managed CI before changing that authority. Do not silently accept a reconstructed roster.

Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only indexes, npm channel promotion, universal registry checksum requirements and automatic wrapper bump severity also need a support/policy decision. The proposed model keeps room for them without making them required implementations.

A failure to stage `pre.json` removal after stable finalization leaves the file in place, and a fresh `version` invocation refuses with E121 and manual recovery guidance. This fail-closed outcome is the selected policy, not an automatic-retry feature; an end-to-end regression verifies it.

The process for using an OIDC publisher is:

  1. Retrieve an OIDC token from the OIDC identity provider;
  2. Submit that token to PyPI, which will return a short-lived API key;
  3. Use that API key as you normally would (e.g. with `twine`)

All code below assumes that it's being run in a GitHub Actions workflow runner with `id-token: write` permissions. That permission is critical; without it, GitHub Actions will refuse to give you an OIDC token.

        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
          id-token: write
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v3

# Publishing to PyPI with a Trusted Publisher

"Trusted Publishing" is our term for using the OpenID Connect (OIDC) standard to exchange short-lived identity tokens between a trusted third-party service and PyPI. This method can be used in automated environments and eliminates the need to use manually generated API tokens to authenticate with PyPI when publishing.

For a quickstart, see:

  * Adding a trusted publisher to an existing PyPI project
  * Creating a PyPI project with a trusted publisher

## Quick background: Publishing with OpenID Connect

OpenID Connect (OIDC) publishing is a mechanism for uploading packages to PyPI, complementing API tokens.

You don't need to understand OIDC to use OIDC publishing with PyPI, but here's the TL;DR:

  1. Certain CI services (like GitHub Actions) are OIDC identity providers, meaning that they can issue short-lived credentials ("OIDC tokens") that a third party can strongly verify came from the CI service (as well as which user, repository, etc. actually executed);
  2. Projects on PyPI can be configured to trust a particular configuration on a particular CI service, making that configuration an OIDC publisher for that project;
  3. Release automation (like GitHub Actions) can submit an OIDC token to PyPI. The token will be matched against configurations trusted by different projects; if any projects trust the token's configuration, then PyPI will mint a short-lived API token for those projects and return it;
  4. The short-lived API token behaves exactly like a normal project-scoped API token, except that it's only valid for 15 minutes from time of creation (enough time for the CI to use it to upload packages).

This confers significant usability and security advantages when compared to PyPI's traditional authentication methods:

  * Usability: with Trusted Publishing, users no longer need to manually create API tokens on PyPI and copy-paste them into their CI provider. The only manual step is configuring the publisher on PyPI.
  * Security: PyPI's normal API tokens are long-lived, meaning that an attacker who compromises a package's release token can use it until its legitimate user notices and manually revokes it. Trusted Publishing avoids this problem because the tokens minted expire automatically.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

When a build is triggered by a user that will publish to PyPI, an OIDC token is generated and passed into the necessary build container as an environment variable along with your release artifact that will be uploaded.

In summary: treat your Trusted Publishers as if they are API tokens. If you wouldn't let a user or piece of code access your API token, then they shouldn't be able to invoke your Trusted Publisher.

## Provider-specific considerations

Each Trusted Publishing provider is its own OIDC identity provider, with its own security model and considerations.

[Input][Input][Input][Input]

GitHub Actions Google Cloud ActiveState GitLab CI/CD

### Security model

GitHub Actions' own security model for OpenID Connect tokens is a little subtle:

  * Any workflow defined in a repository can request an OIDC token, with any audience, so long as it has the `id-token: write` permission.

  * The claims defined in an OIDC token are bound to the workflow, meaning that a workflow defined at `foo.yml` in `org/repo` cannot impersonate a workflow defined at `bar.yml` in `org/repo`. However, if `foo.yml` is renamed to `bar.yml`, then the new `bar.yml` will be indistinguishable from the old `bar.yml` except for claims that reflect the repository's state (e.g. `git` ref, branch, etc.).

  * Generally speaking, "third party" events cannot request an OIDC token: even if they can trigger the workflow that requests the token, the actual token retrieval step will fail. For example: PRs issued from forks of a repository cannot access the OIDC tokens in the "upstream" repository's workflows.

  * The exception to this is `pull_request_target` events, which are fundamentally dangerous by design and should not be used without careful consideration.

### Considerations

  * In particular, for Trusted Publishing with GitHub Actions, you must:

    * Trust the correct username and repository: if you trust a repository other than one you control and trust, that repository can upload to your PyPI project.

    * Trust the correct workflow: you shouldn't trust every workflow to upload to PyPI; instead, you should isolate responsibility to the smallest (and least-privileged) possible separate workflow. We recommend naming this workflow `release.yml`.

    * Take care when merging third-party changes to your code: if you trust `release.yml`, then you must make sure that third-party changes to that workflow (or code that runs within that workflow) are not malicious.

    * Take care when adding repository contributors, members, and administrators: by default, anybody who can unconditionally commit to your repository can also modify your publishing workflow to make it trigger on events you may not intend (e.g., a manual `workflow_dispatch` trigger).

This particular risk can be mitigated by using a dedicated environment with manual approvers, as described below.

## How Trusted Publishing works

PyPI's Trusted Publishing functionality is built on top of OpenID Connect, or "OIDC" for short.

OIDC gives services (like GitHub Actions) a way to provably identify themselves: an authorized entity (such as a GitHub user, or an automated workflow) can present an OIDC token to a third-party service. That party service can then verify the token and determine whether it's authorized to perform some other action.

In the context of Trusted Publishing, the machinery is as follows:

  * OIDC identity providers like GitHub ("providers" for short) generate OIDC tokens that contain scoped claims, which convey appropriate authorization scopes.

    * For example, the `repo` claim might be bound to the value `octo-org/example`, indicating that the token should be authorized to access resources for which `octo-org/example` is a valid repository.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Runs `callisto release` (mode: release) and fills published/publishedPackages
     3	# from its receipt; callisto release's own idempotency makes a redundant run a no-op.
     4	set -euo pipefail
     5	
     6	cd "$INPUT_CWD"
     7	
     8	runtime_dir="$(mktemp -d "${RUNNER_TEMP:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/callisto-release.XXXXXX")"
     9	receipt="$runtime_dir/release-receipt.json"
    10	cleanup() {
    11	  rm -f "$runtime_dir/npmrc" "$receipt"
    12	  rmdir "$runtime_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
    13	}
    14	trap cleanup EXIT
    15	
    16	if [[ -n "${NPM_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
    17	  npm_config="${NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG:-${HOME:-}/.npmrc}"
    18	  if [[ -n "${HOME:-}" && -f "$npm_config" ]]; then
    19	    cp "$npm_config" "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
    20	  else
    21	    : > "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
    22	  fi
    23	  chmod 600 "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
    24	  printf '\n//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}\n' >> "$runtime_dir/npmrc"
    25	  export CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG="$runtime_dir/npmrc"
    26	fi
    27	
    28	if [[ -n "${PYPI_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then
    29	  export TWINE_USERNAME=__token__
    30	  export TWINE_PASSWORD="$PYPI_TOKEN"
    31	  unset PYPI_TOKEN
    32	fi
    33	
    34	output=$(callisto --format json release --receipt "$receipt")
    35	
    36	if jq -e '.nothingToRelease == true' <<< "$output" > /dev/null; then
    37	  echo 'published=false' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    38	  echo 'publishedPackages=[]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    39	  echo '::notice::Nothing to release.'
    40	  exit 0
    41	fi
    42	
    43	packages=$(jq -c '[
    44	    .outcomes[]
    45	    | select(.outcome.kind == "published" and (.operation.role.kind == "registryPublish" or .operation.role.kind == "platformPublish"))
    46	    | .operation.package
    47	  ] | unique' "$receipt")
    48	published=$(jq -r 'length > 0' <<< "$packages")
    49	{
    50	  echo "published=$published"
    51	  echo "publishedPackages=$packages"
    52	} >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

content.text:
## Assessment

I reviewed the two human-authored open PRs: [#232](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/232) and its stacked follow-up, [#233](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/233). GitHub also lists an automated version PR, #221. **The work is strong and addresses a real release-integrity failure**, but I would request a small correction before merging the pair and a hosted release exercise before calling the new path production-proven.

| Priority | Finding | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Medium — #232, inherited by #233** | An unsealed file uploaded in the current run is accepted when the index supplies **no SHA-256**. The comparison only flags a digest *if one exists*; the test explicitly expects this result. That contradicts the PR’s confirmation claim and the [publishing guide](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/docs/publishing.md:98>). See [comparison](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/pypi_files.rs:243>) and [test](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/pypi_files/tests.rs:146>). | Either require SHA-256 for files this run uploaded, as the stated contract says, or explicitly narrow the contract and documentation. A hashless response is permitted by the [Simple Repository API](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/), so this case needs an intentional policy. |
| **Medium — documentation** | [releasing.md](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/docs/releasing.md:114>) still says a partial PyPI upload can be mistaken for a complete release. That is the behavior #232 changes. The [findings register](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md:17>) also describes sealing as unfinished. | Update these current-behavior documents in the PR stack. |
| **Low to medium — performance** | File inventory and the sealed-file recheck read each entire wheel or sdist into memory to hash it. See [inventory and recheck](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/pypi_files.rs:90>). Large wheels can cause avoidable memory spikes. | Use the existing streaming digest pattern used by artifact verification. |

### Engineering judgment

The architecture is thoughtful. The release intent, provider observation, preflight, publish, and confirmation stages have distinct responsibilities. #232 removes the unsafe `dist/*` style upload and makes recovery operate on an explicit file inventory. #233 binds downloaded Python files to a manifest, verifies their bytes, and keeps the matrix build job free of registry credentials. The code also removes known credential variables from Python build subprocesses. Those are meaningful security and maintainability improvements.

The cost is considerable complexity: roughly 2,900 changed lines across the stack, with another durable manifest field and more provider state. I think that complexity is justified for partial-upload recovery, but it raises the value of end-to-end evidence. Both PRs currently have **12 passing GitHub checks**. Their tests cover partial uploads, reruns, yanks, index lag, altered bytes, and manifest validation. The repository also enforces a 90% workspace coverage gate. The remaining limit is that the hosted generated workflow has not run; the existing real-registry tests do not exercise every production binding and observation path.

For publishing practice, Cargo metadata and dependency direction are sound, and Cargo performs package verification during publish; its own guide additionally recommends a pre-publish dry run and package-content inspection. [Cargo publishing guide](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/publishing.html). For npm and PyPI, the generated workflows still use long-lived secrets. Both registries now document trusted publishing with short-lived OIDC credentials; that is a worthwhile future security improvement, especially for a release tool, rather than a defect introduced by these PRs. [npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/), [PyPI trusted publishing](https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/). Python-only generated releases also remain unsealed and build inside the write-capable release job, as #233 clearly discloses.

**My merge recommendation:** fix the hashless-confirmation contract and stale docs, then merge #232 before #233. Treat #233’s generated workflow as promising but not fully validated until one representative hosted build, partial upload, and rerun has succeeded. I made no repository changes.

See [comparison](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/pypi_files.rs:243>) and [test](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/pypi_files/tests.rs:146>). | Either require SHA-256 for files this run uploaded, as the stated contract says, or explicitly narrow the contract and documentation. A hashless response is permitted by the [Simple Repository API](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/simple-repository-api/), so this case needs an intentional policy. |
| **Medium — documentation** | [releasing.md](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/docs/releasing.md:114>) still says a partial PyPI upload can be mistaken for a complete release. That is the behavior #232 changes. The [findings register](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/docs/projects/V1-FINDINGS.md:17>) also describes sealing as unfinished. | Update these current-behavior documents in the PR stack. |
| **Low to medium — performance** | File inventory and the sealed-file recheck read each entire wheel or sdist into memory to hash it. See [inventory and recheck](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/pypi_files.rs:90>). Large wheels can cause avoidable memory spikes. | Use the existing streaming digest pattern used by artifact verification. |

### Engineering judgment

The architecture is thoughtful. The release intent, provider observation, preflight, publish, and confirmation stages have distinct responsibilities. #232 removes the unsafe `dist/*` style upload and makes recovery operate on an explicit file inventory. #233 binds downloaded Python files to a manifest, verifies their bytes, and keeps the matrix build job free of registry credentials. The code also removes known credential variables from Python build subprocesses. Those are meaningful security and maintainability improvements.

The cost is considerable complexity: roughly 2,900 changed lines across the stack, with another durable manifest field and more provider state. I think that complexity is justified for partial-upload recovery, but it raises the value of end-to-end evidence. Both PRs currently have **12 passing GitHub checks**. Their tests cover partial uploads, reruns, yanks, index lag, altered bytes, and manifest validation. The repository also enforces a 90% workspace coverage gate. The remaining limit is that the hosted generated workflow has not run; the existing real-registry tests do not exercise every production binding and observation path.

For publishing practice, Cargo metadata and dependency direction are sound, and Cargo performs package verification during publish; its own guide additionally recommends a pre-publish dry run and package-content inspection. [Cargo publishing guide](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/publishing.html). For npm and PyPI, the generated workflows still use long-lived secrets. Both registries now document trusted publishing with short-lived OIDC credentials; that is a worthwhile future security improvement, especially for a release tool, rather than a defect introduced by these PRs. [npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/), [PyPI trusted publishing](https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/). Python-only generated releases also remain unsealed and build inside the write-capable release job, as #233 clearly discloses.

**My merge recommendation:** fix the hashless-confirmation contract and stale docs, then merge #232 before #233. Treat #233’s generated workflow as promising but not fully validated until one representative hosted build, partial upload, and rerun has succeeded. I made no repository changes.

# V1 system findings

Baseline: main `8ef9aa5a4` (#168), audited on 2026-09-26. This is an open findings register, not an implemented behavior spec. Corrections implemented locally are labeled and remain unshipped until merged. [Roadmap](ROAD-TO-V1.md), [execution guide](V1-IMPLEMENTATION.md), [task definitions](V1-SYSTEM-HARDENING.json), [proposed model](../architecture/polyglot-v1.md).

Confirmed means reproduced against the main binary or established by the cited code path; the evidence column distinguishes them. The earlier isolated run passed 6 identity, 5 schema-guard, 10 release-command and 14 durable-release tests. Those tests do not establish the missing producer/consumer or ecosystem coverage. No full `just ci`, hosted publication, competitor execution or fresh-repo timing run was performed in that audit.

## Implemented locally, awaiting merge

These corrections are not shipped. [Batch verification](V1-VERIFICATION.md) records local results and remaining checks.

| Finding | Correction and evidence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-ENV | Unchanged decide stdout reproduced E281 at the baseline. The CLI accepts the decide report or strict bare wire while preserving typed validation. Review also found strict post-move verification rejected the action's own update with E148; the model now permits only that exact applied-head transition. Real-binary, model and shell action tests cover the boundaries and unrelated-change negatives. | T01 | REL-PR-02, REL-PR-04, REL-PR-07 |
| SYS-INSTALL | Auto installation honors explicit/action-ref versions, including inside Callisto source. Local compilation requires explicit source selection and native workspace ownership checks. Isolated installer fixtures cover consumer names, pins, source rejection and attestation/fallback behavior. | T11 | REL-PR-06 |
| SYS-SCHEMA | Custom string serializers now have string-shaped, named schema definitions. A full JSON Schema validator checks every exposed schema target against real report/durable payloads and malformed nested values; full CI passes. | T02 | CLI-SCHEMA-01, CLI-OUT-05, REL-CMD-12 |
| SYS-PYDEC | Durable release entries, operations, slots and bound registry observations decode versions with the owning distribution's grammar. Genuine Python stable release plan/execute/rerun tests preserve PEP 440 values and reject foreign rosters; independent review found no must-fix. | T03 | REL-AUTH-01/03 |
| SYS-CASCADE | Dependency declarations now retain both local key and native target; graph walking and shared cascade/floor/snapshot rewriting use the declaration's manifest ecosystem. Cargo aliases, inherited root declarations, promoted dual Cargo/npm packages and normalized Python graph names have regressions; independent review cleared T04 and full CI passes. | T04 | VER-CAS-07, VER-PRE-09 |
| SYS-PYPRE | Pre-release baselines now resolve their historical/display identity before native grammar validation. Validation uses the original JSON spelling, so PEP 440 fallback cannot normalize invalid SemVer input; Python stable cycles, promoted/historical keys, malformed values, exit and resume are covered. | T03-PRE | VER-PRE-01/03/06/10 |
| SYS-INHERITED, SYS-ROOT | Historical release verification now reads effective versions from Git blobs, including Cargo workspace inheritance; normalized root/member/changelog paths are checked against the claimed roster. Tests cover authority-only root changes, unclaimed owners and unsafe paths. | T03-HISTORY | REL-AUTH-02, VER-APPLY-13 |
| SYS-PNPM | Dependency state now retains pnpm workspace suffixes, alias targets and relative paths. Explicit SemVer ranges are checked and safely rewritten; aliases preserve keys, relative references resolve only to admitted members, and native pack/frozen-install tests cover version and snapshot flows. | T04-PNPM | WS-ID-10, VER-CAS-05/06 |
| SYS-LOCK | Lockfile refresh and staging now include every actual version/dependency/platform/optional-dependency write ecosystem, including dual manifests and workspace-root Cargo writes. Cross-ecosystem and dependency-only regressions pass in full CI. | T04-LOCK | VER-APPLY-14, VER-PRE-08 |
| SYS-VERSION-RECOVERY | Consumed changesets and pre-state deletions are deferred until lock refresh and generated-state staging succeed. Partial-run detection checks staged effective versions, permits metadata-only edits and handles the examined prerelease exit and inherited-Cargo cases; regressions cover untracked inputs, failed deletion staging, staged/restored versions, exit-state stable bumps, and a fresh E121 refusal after pre-state deletion staging fails. | T05 | VER-APPLY-08/10/13/15/16 |
| SYS-BINS, SYS-NONCARGO | Cargo executable discovery covers explicit and automatic bin targets. npm/Python executables are rejected as unsupported generated artifact builders before writes, while registry-only setup remains available. Focused init and manifest tests plus full CI pass. | T10-BINS | CLI-INIT-01/02/12, CLI-WF-04 |
| SYS-AUTH | Generated release actions configure npm auth in a mode-0600 temporary user config using `${NPM_TOKEN}` interpolation (the secret is not written to disk), map PyPI credentials to Twine, support Bun's token contract, and filter release credentials including `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` from Python build subprocesses. Native package-manager lifecycle hooks retain normal package-owner-defined behavior; Callisto does not suppress or rewrite them. Fake-tool and environment-filter tests pass; generated workflow tests keep secrets out of version-pr/plan/build. | T10-AUTH | CLI-WF-03/04; ADR 4 |

## Open confirmed defects

| Finding | Evidence and consequence | Plan | Contract/area |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SYS-OWNER | `sole_owner_at`: current first-manifest path existence is not historic name/full-roster ownership. Reproduced loss of a bare tag after sibling rename or addition of a new primary canonical manifest. | T06-HISTORY | WS-ID-03; historical migration |
| SYS-DEMOTION | `tags.rs`: removing a same-named sibling loses a newer qualified tag and chooses an older bare release. Reproduced; inference can replay already-released work. | T06-HISTORY | WS-ID-03; historical migration |
| SYS-RETRY | `derive_unreleased_decision`: local tags exclude a package before remaining operations are observed. Reproduced tag creation followed by push failure, then exit 0 with `Nothing to release.` and no receipt. Generated simple CI uses this path; Callisto's own committed-roster CI does not. | T08-RETRY | REL-RERUN-02; REL-CMD-01/08 need coordinated selection changes |
| SYS-BARRIER | `release/derive.rs`: a dual Cargo/npm owner creates a shared physical tag/GitHub publication after one distribution but before the other's publish. Reproduced plan ordering; per-distribution gates do not enforce the owner's completion barrier. | T08 | REL-ORD-01 |
| SYS-NAPI | `commands/init.rs`: generated native builds and placement use workspace-wide napi selection rather than the verified intent. An unrelated addon can block a Cargo-only release. Source-confirmed. | T10 | CLI-WF-04; committed roster authority |
| SYS-MATURIN | `Package::version_grammar`: two fresh co-located Cargo/Maturin repos, with matching static versions and Cargo-owned dynamic Python versions, both reproduce E007 from init/status. Separate-directory fixtures did not cover this layout. | T07 | WS-ID-09; proposed version authority |
| SYS-PYFILES | `provider/registry.rs` returns Exact for any matching non-yanked Python file; `provider/mod.rs` adopts it as AlreadySatisfied. `registry_argv.rs` builds both wheel and sdist. Source-confirmed partial-upload retry gap; no live fault-injection run yet. | T09 | REL-PUB-04/08, REL-RERUN-01/04 |
| SYS-PYROUTES | `PreparedRegistryBinding.endpoint` is reused for simple-index observation and Twine upload. Source-confirmed single-route assumption; servers with distinct read/upload routes cannot generally use one override. Public defaults use separate native routes. | T09-ROUTES | REL-PUB-04/08; private-index policy |

## Integration risks and evidence gaps

- Status changeset attribution and well-formedness checks still scan display ids through `PackageId::resolve_unique`, while version aggregation uses `IdentityIndex::resolve_id`. Source-visible resolver divergence can reject a valid secondary native name or accept an unrelated qualified selector. Add a paired status/version fixture and migrate both status helpers with the other selector consumers (T06).
- Native npm lifecycle hooks can initiate effects outside Callisto's release-operation graph. Their behavior is package-owner-defined and is not inspected, rewritten, suppressed or rejected by Callisto; this is an explicit ownership boundary, not an automatic-enforcement defect.
- Registry version existence is not proof of identical package bytes, complete Python files or the desired npm dist-tag. Artifact-set completion is a correctness fix (T09); universal checksum enforcement and channel promotion remain owner decisions.
- PyPI yanking is per file. The current classifier treats any matching yanked file as Absent even alongside non-yanked files. A yank is not deletion or permission to overwrite; confirm conflict/partial semantics with the required-output model (T09).
- Cargo and PyPI real local registry tests exist in `release_real_registry_e2e_tests.rs`; they drive publisher argv directly, bypass production binding/observation in those paths, and can skip when tools are missing. npm has broader end-to-end coverage. Record exercised versus skipped paths; do not mark the missing Cargo test as the remaining v1 blocker (T12).
- Fresh local Cargo/npm/PyPI repositories completed documented setup through release dry-run; npm packing and Cargo package inventory passed. Python artifact build was blocked on sandbox network access to `setuptools`, and no timings, credentials, registry publication or hosted release were exercised. The under-ten-minute first-published-release goal therefore remains unverified (T12-DX).
- Go v2/tag publication and NuGet normalized versions/RID/TFM assets are architecture examples only, not production support or new v1 gates (T07/T08/T12).

## Owner policy, not a defect verdict

Commit inference can produce pending bumps while `hasChangesets` is false; managed release-PR decisions then return noop. Committed verification also requires a consumed changeset, as ADR 2 states. Decide whether inferred-only/manual version releases belong in managed CI before changing that authority. Do not silently accept a reconstructed roster.

Authenticated private PyPI/HTML-only indexes, npm channel promotion, universal registry checksum requirements and automatic wrapper bump severity also need a support/policy decision. The proposed model keeps room for them without making them required implementations.

A failure to stage `pre.json` removal after stable finalization leaves the file in place, and a fresh `version` invocation refuses with E121 and manual recovery guidance. This fail-closed outcome is the selected policy, not an automatic-retry feature; an end-to-end regression verifies it.

## v0.9 handoff

Merge the verified T01 correction to unblock release-PR refresh. Then require fresh release-source/decision agreement and passing workflow checks before merging the refreshed PR; do not merge the stale #113 decision as a workaround. [Run 36281315129](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/actions/runs/36281315129) records the E281 failure that prevented refresh after later merges. No claim that E281 is the only possible publication blocker is established until the actual self-release succeeds.

The publication intent, artifact-manifest and receipt files are written without the stdout report envelope, so the same wrapper mismatch was not found there. That source inspection does not replace executing the publish path.

1	//! Raw HTTP response parsing for the forge lookups that go through
     2	//! `gh api --include`.
     3	//!
     4	//! The response is kept whole -- status line, headers, body -- because the
     5	//! retry policy needs `Retry-After` and the rate-limit headers, and the
     6	//! classifier needs the exact status.

     8	use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

    10	/// One parsed HTTP response.
    11	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    12	pub(crate) struct HttpResponse {
    13	    pub(crate) status: u16,
    14	    pub(crate) headers: Vec<(String, String)>,
    15	    pub(crate) body: String,
    16	}
    17	
    18	impl HttpResponse {
    19	    pub(crate) fn header(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    20	        self.headers
    21	            .iter()
    22	            .find(|(key, _)| key.eq_ignore_ascii_case(name))
    23	            .map(|(_, value)| value.as_str())
    24	    }

I found three additional issues in the current PR stack. I can establish them from the code, but I cannot verify whether Claude previously noticed them: the saved Entire history is unavailable in this session.

1. **High — a Python-only build runs while Git has write credentials.** The generated [simple release workflow](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/templates/simple_workflow.tmpl:21>) gives the job `contents: write` and checks out with persisted credentials. An unsealed release runs the project’s Python build backend in that job. The [build subprocess](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/registry.rs:293>) removes credential *environment variables*, which is good, but a backend can still run authenticated Git commands: [actions/checkout documents](https://github.com/actions/checkout) that persisted credentials keep `git push` working. This is a supply-chain exposure if a build backend or its dependency is compromised. The new credential-free `build-python` job closes this path for matrix releases, but Python-only generated releases remain on the simple route. I would isolate their build too, or make Git credentials available only after building.

2. **Medium — pnpm discovery and publishing disagree.** Workspace detection recognizes either `pnpm-lock.yaml` **or** `pnpm-workspace.yaml` in [npm.rs](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-manifests/src/npm.rs:625>). The publish selector recognizes only the lockfile in [registry_argv.rs](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/registry_argv.rs:161>). A valid pnpm workspace with its workspace file but no lockfile is discovered as pnpm, then published with `npm publish --workspace=...`. That can fail to select the package or use different packing behavior. The two paths should share one package-manager decision.

3. **Medium — a malformed sealed Python filename fails late.** [Manifest validation](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-model/src/release/artifact.rs:276>) checks the Python roster, safe names, and wheel/sdist extensions, but does not check that each filename belongs to its declared package and version. [Byte verification](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_artifacts.rs:111>) likewise accepts a matching file. The ownership check occurs when the [PyPI file set is constructed](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/pypi_files.rs:137>) during that operation. In a mixed release, another eligible publish can therefore land before a bad Python manifest is rejected. Validate every sealed filename before the executor starts effects.

A smaller issue: [NAPI target drift detection](</Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.claude/worktrees/pypi-sealed-set/crates/callisto-graph/src/napi.rs:14>) guesses `root/<package-name>/package.json`. Packages under `packages/` or with scoped names will skip the cross-check. This affects a warning, not the primary release operation.

These are separate from the hashless PyPI confirmation defect I reported earlier. This was a targeted read-only audit of the PR head and adjacent paths, not a claim that the rest of the repository is defect-free; I did not run a hosted publication or add reproducing tests.
